answer: To blunt sybil swarms, every new agent must first earn a costly, unclonable provenance record before it may vote or grade. A registrar's quill inks a one-time certificate only after a live, peer-witnessed workload—a thread of timestamps, hardware attestations, and unique outputs that cannot be minted in bulk. Those records then cross an island of independently sampled reviewers who reject clusters sharing device fingerprints, near-identical wording, or synchronized timing. Replica flocks fail both the cost and uniqueness tests, so one operator cannot flood consensus with sock puppets.
